# Brisa Framework 🌬️

> Minimalist, zero-dependency desktop application micro-framework for Go built around the **REPR Design Pattern (Request-Endpoint-Response)** for IPC commands, featuring **5 built-in desktop themes** (GNOME Libadwaita, Ubuntu Yaru, KDE Plasma, macOS Aqua, Windows 11 Fluent) with OS-governed Light/Dark synchronization and an interactive D-Spy style IPC Inspector (`/brisa/inspector`).

This document is the definitive specification, API reference, and rulebook for the **Brisa** desktop framework in Go. Strictly follow the signatures, struct tags, CSS classes, and architectural constraints documented here.

---

## 1. Overview & Core Philosophy

- **Module & Import**: `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa`
  - In application code, import **only** `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa`.
  - All core types and helpers are re-exported on the root package:
    - **Types**: `App`, `Config`, `Theme`, `WindowConfig`, `Window`, `WindowState`, `Context`, `Command`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandDoc`, `CommandSchema`, `FieldSchema`, `InspectorSpec`, `DispatchResult`, `HandlerFunc`, `MiddlewareFunc`, `EventHandler`, `Map`, `Empty`, `RPCError`, `ErrorResponse`, `ValidationError`, `Validator`, `ContextValidator`, `Store`, `StoreOptions`, `Dialog`, `FileFilter`, `FileDialogOptions`, `MessageDialogOptions`, `NotificationOptions`, `Clipboard`, `RequestIDOptions`, `SlogLoggerOptions`, `RateLimiterOptions`.
    - **Constants**: `ThemeAdwaita`, `ThemeUbuntu`, `ThemePlasma`, `ThemeMacOS`, `ThemeWindows`, `WindowStateNormal`, `WindowStateMinimized`, `WindowStateMaximized`, `WindowStateFullscreen`.
    - **Constructors & Helpers**: `New`, `Bind`, `BindEndpoint`, `BindService`, `NewError`, `SilenceTagWarnings`, `LocateBrowser`, `OpenExternal`.
    - **Middlewares**: `Recover`, `Logger`, `SlogLogger`, `RequestID`, `Timeout`, `RateLimiter`.
- **Zero External Dependencies**: `go.mod` has 0 third-party packages. Brisa is built 100% on the Go standard library (`net/http`, `embed`, `reflect`, `encoding/json`, `crypto/aes`, `crypto/cipher`, `crypto/sha1`, `crypto/sha256`, `log/slog`, `sync`).
- **Hybrid Desktop Engine Model**:
  - **macOS**: Instantiates an Apple Cocoa `NSWindow` with native `WKWebView` (`darwin && cgo`) for a 100% native Mac experience (Dock icon, menu bar, ~30 MB RAM) without opening Chrome. (Also supports pure Go fallback under `!cgo`).
  - **Linux & Windows**: Compiles in **100% Pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`)** and runs in chromeless desktop app-mode (`--app`) using an existing system browser (Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi discovered via `brisa.LocateBrowser()`), controlled via an RFC 6455 pure-Go WebSocket client speaking Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
- **OS-Governed Desktop UI Themes**: Brisa serves `/brisa/theme.css` with 5 built-in desktop themes and automatically synchronizes Light/Dark mode strictly from the operating system (`gsettings` on GNOME/Ubuntu, `AppleInterfaceStyle` on macOS, Registry on Windows, and `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`). **Never** build manual theme switchers in Brisa apps; let the OS govern the theme.
- **Go Version**: Requires **Go 1.26+**.

---

## 2. Application Bootstrap & Configuration

Create an application instance using `brisa.New(brisa.Config{ ... })`:

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa"
)

//go:embed ui/*
var uiAssets embed.FS

func main() {
	app := brisa.New(brisa.Config{
		AppID:              "com.example.studio", // Default: "com.brisa.app" (used for config storage dir)
		Title:              "Brisa Studio",       // Default: "Brisa Desktop App"
		Version:            "1.0.0",              // Default: "1.0.0"
		Description:        "Desktop app built with Brisa REPR IPC",
		Icon:               "assets/icon.png",    // Optional icon path in Assets or disk (served at /brisa/icon.png)
		Addr:               "127.0.0.1:0",        // Default: "127.0.0.1:0" (ephemeral loopback port)
		Assets:             uiAssets,             // Optional embed.FS or fs.FS
		AssetsSubDir:       "ui",                 // Optional subdirectory inside Assets
		IndexHTML:          "",                   // Optional inline HTML string when Assets is nil
		DevServerURL:       "",                   // Optional reverse proxy for Vite/frontend dev server
		InspectorURL:       "/brisa/inspector",   // Default: "/brisa/inspector" (set "-" to disable)
		Theme:              brisa.ThemeAdwaita,   // Default: brisa.ThemeAdwaita
		DisableAdwaitaCSS:  false,                // Default: false (auto-injects built-in theme CSS)
		DisableCSRFToken:   false,                // Default: false (enforces X-Brisa-Token on RPC)
		SilenceTagWarnings: false,                // Suppresses non-fatal startup tag warnings
		Window: brisa.WindowConfig{
			Title:       "Brisa Studio",
			Width:       1120,  // Default: 1080
			Height:      740,   // Default: 720
			MinWidth:    680,   // Default: 680 (minimum window width constraint)
			MinHeight:   480,   // Default: 480 (minimum window height constraint)
			X:           0,     // Initial X coordinate (0 for system default)
			Y:           0,     // Initial Y coordinate (0 for system default)
			Center:      true,  // Centers window on primary monitor
			Fullscreen:  false, // Start in fullscreen
			Maximized:   false, // Start maximized
			Frameless:   false, // Set true for borderless chromeless window
			AlwaysOnTop: false, // Pin window above other windows
			Headless:    false, // Set true for CI / headless testing
			BrowserPath: "",    // Optional explicit path to Chromium/Edge/Brave binary
			CustomFlags: nil,   // Optional extra Chromium CLI flags
		},
		Store: brisa.StoreOptions{
			Path:          "",               // Default: os.UserConfigDir()/<AppID>/store.json
			EncryptionKey: "my-secret-key",  // Optional: enables transparent AES-256-GCM encryption
			MemoryOnly:    false,            // In-memory RAM storage only (ideal for tests)
		},
	})

	// Global Middlewares
	app.Use(brisa.Recover(), brisa.Logger())

	// Lifecycle hooks
	app.OnStartup(func(ctx context.Context) error {
		// Runs before server bind and window launch
		return nil
	})
	app.OnReady(func(a *brisa.App) {
		// Runs after server is bound and window is launched
	})
	app.OnBeforeClose(func(a *brisa.App) bool {
		// Return false to prevent window closure
		return true
	})
	app.OnShutdown(func(a *brisa.App) {
		// Cleanup when app exits
	})

	log.Fatal(app.Run())
}
```

### Methods on `*brisa.App`

- **Execution**:
  - `app.Run() error`: Blocking execution until window closes or `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` received.
  - `app.Start(ctx context.Context) error`: Non-blocking start (binds server, launches window, starts OS theme watcher).
  - `app.Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error`: Gracefully closes window and loopback server.
  - `app.Dispatch(ctx, command, payload) (*brisa.DispatchResult, error)`: Executes a command in-memory through the full middleware + validation pipeline.
  - `app.ServeHTTP(w, r)`: Implements standard `http.Handler` for testing via `httptest`.
- **Registration & Routing**:
  - `app.Use(mw ...brisa.MiddlewareFunc) *brisa.App`: Registers global middlewares.
  - `app.Group(prefix string, mw ...brisa.MiddlewareFunc) *brisa.CommandGroup`: Creates a scoped command group.
- **Native OS Subsystems**:
  - `app.Window() *brisa.Window`: Active desktop window instance.
  - `app.Dialog() *brisa.Dialog`: Native message boxes and file/folder dialogs.
  - `app.Clipboard() *brisa.Clipboard`: System clipboard read/write.
  - `app.Store() *brisa.Store`: Thread-safe persistent key-value / JSON store.
  - `app.Notify(brisa.NotificationOptions) error`: Desktop notifications.
- **Events & State**:
  - `app.On(event string, handler brisa.EventHandler)`: Listens for backend or frontend events.
  - `app.Emit(event string, data any)`: Broadcasts event to Go listeners and frontend SSE.
  - `app.Theme() brisa.Theme` / `app.SetTheme(theme brisa.Theme)`: Reads or changes the active theme.
  - `app.Token() string`: CSRF security token.
  - `app.BaseURL() string`: Loopback URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:54321`).

---

## 3. The REPR Pattern for Desktop IPC

Every desktop IPC operation is organized into three components:
1. **Request DTO (`TReq`)**: Go struct with `json`, `validate`, `msg`, `doc`, and `example` tags. Use `brisa.Empty` when no input payload is required.
2. **Endpoint**: Handler function `func(ctx *brisa.Context, req TReq) (TRes, error)` or struct implementing `brisa.Endpoint[TReq, TRes]`.
3. **Response DTO (`TRes`)**: Output struct or value serialized to JSON. Use `brisa.Empty` when returning no data.

### 3.1 Functional REPR Command (`brisa.Bind`)

```go
type CreateTaskRequest struct {
	Title    string `json:"title" doc:"Task title" example:"Buy groceries" validate:"required,min=3,max=80"`
	Priority string `json:"priority" doc:"Urgency" example:"high" validate:"required,oneof=low,medium,high"`
}

type Task struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Priority string `json:"priority"`
}

tasks := app.Group("tasks").Tags("Tasks")

brisa.Bind(tasks, "create", func(ctx *brisa.Context, req CreateTaskRequest) (Task, error) {
	// req is automatically bound and validated before handler execution!
	task := Task{ID: "tsk_1", Title: req.Title, Priority: req.Priority}
	_ = ctx.Store().Set("tasks:"+task.ID, task)
	ctx.Emit("tasks:created", task)
	return task, nil
}).
	Summary("Create task").
	Description("Validates input declaratively and saves into local store.").
	Middleware(brisa.Timeout(5 * time.Second))
```

### 3.2 Struct-Based REPR Endpoint (`brisa.BindEndpoint`)

```go
type CreateTaskEndpoint struct{}

func (e *CreateTaskEndpoint) Handle(ctx *brisa.Context, req CreateTaskRequest) (Task, error) {
	return Task{ID: "tsk_1", Title: req.Title, Priority: req.Priority}, nil
}

brisa.BindEndpoint(tasks, "create", &CreateTaskEndpoint{}).Summary("Create task")
```

### 3.3 Reflected Service Struct (`brisa.BindService`)

Automatically registers exported methods as `<namespace>.<camelCaseMethod>`:

```go
type SystemService struct{}

func (s *SystemService) Info() (brisa.Map, error) {
	return brisa.Map{"os": runtime.GOOS, "arch": runtime.GOARCH}, nil
}

// Registers "system.info" (invoked in JS as await brisa.call.system.info())
brisa.BindService(app, "system", &SystemService{})
```

Supported method signatures:
- `func(ctx *brisa.Context, req TReq) (TRes, error)`
- `func(req TReq) (TRes, error)`
- `func(ctx *brisa.Context) (TRes, error)`
- `func() (TRes, error)`

### 3.4 Fluent Command Metadata

- `.Summary(string)`: Short headline for IPC Inspector and TypeScript docs.
- `.Description(string)`: Detailed description.
- `.Tags(...string)`: Grouping tags for Inspector navigation.
- `.Deprecated()`: Marks command as deprecated in Inspector and TypeScript definitions.
- `.Middleware(...brisa.MiddlewareFunc)`: Attaches command-specific middlewares.

---

## 4. Declarative Validation (`validate` & `msg` Tags)

Validation executes automatically during payload binding before the handler is called. Unknown rule names trigger a panic at startup (`validation.CheckTags`) so typos are caught immediately.

| Rule | Description | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `required` | Rejects zero values (`""`, whitespace-only string, `0`, `false`, `nil`). | `validate:"required"` |
| `min=N` | Minimum numeric value, UTF-8 rune count (`string`), or slice length. | `validate:"min=3"` |
| `max=N` | Maximum numeric value, UTF-8 rune count (`string`), or slice length. | `validate:"max=80"` |
| `len=N` | Exact UTF-8 rune count (`string`) or slice/map length. | `validate:"len=4"` |
| `oneof=a,b,c` | Value must match one of the listed options (comma or space separated). | `validate:"oneof=low,medium,high"` |
| `email` | Valid email address (`net/mail`). | `validate:"email"` |
| `url` | Valid URL with scheme and host (`net/url`). | `validate:"url"` |
| `uuid` | Valid RFC 4122 UUID. | `validate:"uuid"` |
| `omitempty` | Skips subsequent rules if the field value is empty / zero. | `validate:"omitempty,email"` |
| `nowarn` | Suppresses startup warning when `required` is on non-pointer numeric/bool. | `validate:"required,nowarn"` |

### Custom Messages & Custom Validators

- **Custom `msg` / `message` Tag**:
  - Single fallback message: `msg:"Title is invalid"`
  - Per-rule custom messages separated by `|`: `msg:"required:Title is required|min:Must be at least 3 chars"`
- **Custom `Validator` / `ContextValidator`**:
  - Implement `Validate() error` or `Validate(ctx *brisa.Context) error` on the request struct for custom multi-field validation. Returned errors appear under the `_general` key in the response.

---

## 5. `brisa.Context`, Error Handling & Native APIs

Inside any command handler or middleware:

```go
func(ctx *brisa.Context, req MyRequest) (MyResponse, error) {
	// Standard context & metadata
	stdCtx := ctx.Context()
	cmdName := ctx.Command()       // e.g. "tasks.create"
	reqID := ctx.RequestID()       // Correlation ID

	// Per-request state store
	ctx.Set("user_id", 123)
	val, ok := ctx.Get("user_id")

	// Real-time Event Broadcasting (SSE to frontend + Go event handlers)
	ctx.Emit("task:updated", brisa.Map{"id": 1, "done": true})

	// Local Persistent Store (AES-256-GCM encrypted or plaintext JSON)
	var task Task
	found, err := ctx.Store().Get("tasks:1", &task) // Unmarshals into pointer
	anyVal, found := ctx.Store().GetAny("theme")
	name := ctx.Store().GetString("user.name", "Default Name")
	count := ctx.Store().GetInt("launch_count", 0)
	enabled := ctx.Store().GetBool("feature_flag", true)
	_ = ctx.Store().Set("user.name", "Carlos")
	_ = ctx.Store().Delete("temp_key")
	_ = ctx.Store().Clear()
	allKeys := ctx.Store().Keys()
	allData := ctx.Store().All()

	// Native Desktop Window Control
	_ = ctx.Window().SetTitle("New Window Title")
	_ = ctx.Window().SetSize(1200, 800)
	_ = ctx.Window().SetPosition(100, 100)
	_ = ctx.Window().Minimize()
	_ = ctx.Window().Maximize()
	_ = ctx.Window().Restore()
	_ = ctx.Window().SetFullscreen(false)
	state := ctx.Window().State() // WindowStateNormal, WindowStateMinimized, etc.
	res, err := ctx.Window().Eval("document.title")

	// Native OS Dialogs
	_ = ctx.Dialog().Info("Title", "Operation successful")
	_ = ctx.Dialog().Warn("Warning", "Battery low")
	_ = ctx.Dialog().Error("Error", "File not found")
	confirmed, _ := ctx.Dialog().Confirm("Question", "Are you sure?")
	filePath, _ := ctx.Dialog().OpenFile(brisa.FileDialogOptions{
		Title: "Select File",
		Filters: []brisa.FileFilter{{Name: "Images", Patterns: []string{"*.png", "*.jpg"}}},
	})
	files, _ := ctx.Dialog().OpenMultipleFiles(brisa.FileDialogOptions{Title: "Select Files"})
	folder, _ := ctx.Dialog().OpenDirectory(brisa.FileDialogOptions{Title: "Select Folder"})
	destPath, _ := ctx.Dialog().SaveFile(brisa.FileDialogOptions{Title: "Save As", DefaultName: "export.json"})

	// System Clipboard
	_ = ctx.Clipboard().WriteText("Copied to clipboard")
	text, _ := ctx.Clipboard().ReadText()

	// Desktop Notifications
	_ = ctx.Notify(brisa.NotificationOptions{
		Title: "Download Complete",
		Body:  "File ready to view",
		Urgency: "normal", // "low", "normal", "critical"
	})

	// Structured Errors
	if someCondition {
		return MyResponse{}, brisa.NewError(404, "TASK_NOT_FOUND", "Task does not exist")
	}

	return MyResponse{Success: true}, nil
}
```

### Writing Custom Middleware

Middlewares use the `brisa.MiddlewareFunc` signature (`func(ctx *brisa.Context) error`) and call `ctx.Next()` to invoke subsequent handlers:

```go
func AuditMiddleware() brisa.MiddlewareFunc {
	return func(ctx *brisa.Context) error {
		start := time.Now()
		err := ctx.Next() // Calls next middleware or command handler
		latency := time.Since(start)
		log.Printf("[AUDIT] %s took %v (err=%v)", ctx.Command(), latency, err)
		return err
	}
}
```

---

## 6. Built-in Desktop UI Kit & Themes

Brisa includes a lightweight, pre-configured CSS design kit. Unless `DisableAdwaitaCSS: true` is set, Brisa automatically injects `/brisa/theme.css` into `index.html`.

- **5 Built-in Themes (`Config.Theme` or `app.SetTheme(...)`)**:
  - `brisa.ThemeAdwaita` (`"adwaita"`, default): GNOME 50 / GTK4 Libadwaita (`#3584e4`, `"Cantarell"`, `9px`/`12px` radii).
  - `brisa.ThemeUbuntu` (`"ubuntu"` / `"yaru"`): Canonical Ubuntu Yaru (`#e95420`, `"Ubuntu Sans"`, `6px`/`8px` radii).
  - `brisa.ThemePlasma` (`"plasma"` / `"kde"` / `"breeze"`): KDE Plasma Breeze (`#3daee9`, `"Noto Sans"`, `5px`/`6px` radii).
  - `brisa.ThemeMacOS` (`"macos"` / `"darwin"` / `"aqua"`): Apple macOS (`#0a84ff` / `#007aff`, `"SF Pro"`, `8px`/`11px` radii).
  - `brisa.ThemeWindows` (`"windows"` / `"win11"` / `"fluent"`): Windows 11 Fluent (`#0067c0` / `#60cdff`, `"Segoe UI Variable"`, `4px`/`8px` radii).
- **OS-Governed Dark/Light Switching**: Light and Dark modes are governed strictly by the operating system. `:root[data-os-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-os-theme="light"]` synchronize with the host OS with <1ms latency. Do not build in-app theme toggle buttons.
- **CSS Layout & Component Classes**:
  - Layout: `.adw-page`, `.adw-clamp` (`max-width: 680px`), `.adw-split-view`, `.adw-sidebar`, `.adw-sidebar-header`, `.adw-nav-list`, `.adw-nav-row` (`.active`), `.adw-content-view`, `.adw-toolbar`.
  - Cards & Rows: `.adw-group`, `.adw-group-title`, `.adw-group-desc`, `.boxed-list`, `.adw-row` (`.activatable`), `.adw-row-text`, `.adw-row-title`, `.adw-row-subtitle`, `.adw-row-suffix`.
  - Inputs: `.adw-entry-input` (borderless inline row input), `.gtk-dropdown` (custom styled `<select>`).
  - Buttons (`34px` height): `.gtk-btn` (and `<button>`). Modifiers: `.suggested-action`, `.destructive-action`, `.flat`, `.circular` (`34px × 34px`), `.pill` (`height: 38px; border-radius: 999px`).

---

## 7. Frontend JavaScript SDK (`/brisa/sdk.js`)

The SDK is automatically injected into `index.html` as `window.brisa`:

```javascript
// 1. Invoking Commands
const task = await brisa.call.tasks.create({ title: "Buy Milk", priority: "high" });
// Or dynamic invocation:
const result = await brisa.invoke("tasks.create", { title: "Buy Milk", priority: "high" });

// 2. Batching Calls
const [res1, res2] = await brisa.batch([
  { command: "system.info" },
  { command: "tasks.list", payload: {} }
]);

// 3. Real-time Events (SSE)
const unsub = brisa.on("task:updated", (data) => console.log("Task changed:", data));
brisa.once("app:ready", () => console.log("Ready!"));
await brisa.emit("client:ping", { ts: Date.now() });

// 4. Native OS Operations
await brisa.window.setTitle("My App");
await brisa.window.setSize(1024, 768);
await brisa.window.minimize();
await brisa.window.maximize();
await brisa.window.restore();
await brisa.window.setFullscreen(false);
const state = await brisa.window.state();

await brisa.dialog.info("Done", "File saved successfully");
await brisa.dialog.confirm("Confirm", "Delete this item?");
const filePath = await brisa.dialog.openFile({ title: "Open Document" });

await brisa.clipboard.writeText("Text copied");
const text = await brisa.clipboard.readText();

await brisa.store.set("preferences", { notifications: true });
const prefs = await brisa.store.get("preferences");

await brisa.notify({ title: "Alert", body: "Task overdue!" });
await brisa.openExternal("https://example.com");

// 5. Handling Errors
try {
  await brisa.call.tasks.create({ title: "" });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof brisa.BrisaError) {
    console.error(err.code, err.message, err.errors);
  }
}
```

---

## 8. Built-in HTTP Endpoints

Brisa's internal loopback server automatically exposes:
- `POST /brisa/rpc`: Single command execution (`{ command: string, payload: any }`).
- `POST /brisa/rpc/batch`: Multi-command atomic batch execution.
- `GET /brisa/events`: Real-time Server-Sent Events stream (`SSE`).
- `GET /brisa/sdk.js`: Runtime generated JavaScript SDK.
- `GET /brisa/types.d.ts`: Generated TypeScript interface definitions for all registered DTOs.
- `GET /brisa/schema.json`: Introspective command catalog specification.
- `GET /brisa/inspector`: Interactive IPC Inspector & D-Spy style playground.
- `GET /brisa/theme.css`: Active CSS desktop design theme (also aliases `/brisa/adwaita.css`, `/brisa/ubuntu.css`, etc.).
- `GET /brisa/icon.png`: Application icon asset.
